37113640.extract:
Erik Campbell is a character in the supernatural horror film "Final Destination Bloodlines" (2025), the sixth installment in the Final Destination franchise. He is a main character in the film, introduced as the son of Brenda Campbell and a step-grandson of Paul and Iris Campbell. Erik is a child of Brenda Campbell, an assumed eldest son of Howard and Brenda Campbell, and the older brother of Bobby and Julia Campbell. He was created by Guy Busick, Lori Evans Taylor, and Jon Watts and portrayed by Richard Harmon.

Erik Campbell is a rebellious and bold character. He has a sarcastic sense of humor, wears black clothes, has many piercings and tattoos, and doesn't believe in the supernatural. He works as a tattoo artist and is known for his protective and caring nature towards his family. Erik's character is central to the filmmakers' goal of subverting the audience's expectations, and he plays a crucial role in the plot of the film.

Erik Campbell's character is notable for his unique background and the way he is added to the family tree. He is the only character in the franchise who was never meant to die, which adds a layer of complexity to the story. In the film, Erik faces a dangerous situation and ultimately sacrifices his life to save his family, leading to a dramatic and memorable death.

4.title: Final Destination Bloodlines: Why Erik is Special
4.description: Erik Campbell from Final Destination Bloodlines has stolen our hearts with his sarcastic humor and soft spot for his family.
4.content:
**Let’s be honest, every horror movie needs their laidback, cool alternative character that sticks out no matter how little screen time they get. Sadly, this genre of character tends to die early in the story, usually in a brutal way. And though Erik Campbell gets his unhappy ending, we can appreciate [Final Destination Bloodlines](https://www.trillmag.com/entertainment/tv-film/final-destination-bloodlines-a-new-era-begins-after-a-14-year-hiatus/)for keeping him around long enough.**

_Jennifer’s Body_‘s Colin Gray awakened a lot of fans’ attraction towards alternative characters, mainly those existing in horror settings. Though, they usually don’t serve much of a purpose other than being mysterious with morbid one-liners. An example is Kim Diamond from _Book of Shadows: Blair Witch 2_ who is shown at the beginning of the film smoking a cigarette in a graveyard.

_Final Destination 3_ was the first movie of the franchise that introduced their first ‘goth’ characters Ian and Erin. This trope was popularized in the early 2000s and _Final Destination_ _Bloodlines_ brought it back with our beloved Erik Campbell. But Erik isn’t just there for comic relief, he is a testament to how Death loves to toy with his victims in the franchise. He is also the only character in _Final Destination_ that was supposed to live.

Erik Campbell: The black sheep
------------------------------

![Image 1: Erik Campbell](blob:http://localhost/b7c136f3bc6e2ac1dadad129a9376cf6)

Erik Campbell. (Credit: Warner Bros.)

With his dark hair and sarcastic humor, Erik Campbell bears a resemblance to Ian Mckinley from _Final Destination 3_. Initially, Ian expresses skepticism about the protagonist’s ‘psychic’ ability to predict death. But after witnessing his girlfriend’s death, his disbelief turned him cynical.

Similarly, in _Final Destination Bloodlines_, Erik is skeptical of his cousin Stefani’s premonitions. Instead, he takes Stefani’s warnings as insensitive, especially after his father’s death. Here, he takes on the protective elder sibling role: standing his ground for the family. It’s clear that despite his deadpan nature, Erik cares deeply for his family. He is very much the ‘black sheep’ and yet the film strays away from boxing him into a stereotypical category, giving him a fleshed out arc instead.

“When people see the way I look as Erik, and see the tattoos and piercings that they put on me, they make an assumption about every other alt-looking emo, punk-rock character that we’ve seen played in the genre since the ’80s, you know?” actor Richard Harmon tells [Indiewire](https://www.indiewire.com/features/interviews/final-destination-bloodlines-richard-harmon-interview-1235124193/) about his character Erik. “I knew then that he cared about his family more than anything. That’s actually Erik’s driving force, which I don’t know if it originally was supposed to be.”

Death has a sense of humor
--------------------------

![Image 2: Erik Campbell in Final Destination](blob:http://localhost/30f81a335ede3b5bbd1b498cae00e0a7)

Credit: Warner Bros.

Erik is grieving the death of his father after his shift at the tattoo parlor when a chain of little accidents lead to his near death experience. We soon learn why Erik was spared by death when Mrs. Campbell reveals he has a different father than his siblings. This means he won’t be affected by the Campbell family’s doomed bloodline. So then why would Death waste its time targeting Erik? Was it just to toy with him? Give him a warning?

Directors Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein have admitted that Death is a sentient character throughout the franchise. “Death has a sense of playfulness,” [Stein says about the tattoo parlor scene.](https://www.polygon.com/horror/602031/final-destination-bloodlines-ending-explained-directors-spoilers-erik-death)“Just like a fisherman might catch a fish without intending to kill it, and they’ll hook the fish and then throw ’em back, that’s exactly what Death is doing with Eric in that tattoo parlor scene…”

This analogy is also shown when Erik mocks death in the next scene. As he steps onto the street, he gets narrowly missed by a truck, a reference to a similar scene in the first _Final Destination_. It’s almost like a stern warning from Death. But due to Erik’s determination in trying to save his brother Bobby, Erik ends up paying the consequences. “Tony says it: when you fuck with death, things get messy.” What makes Erik such a special character is that he is the only character in the franchise that is not supposed to die. Still, he is an example of why you shouldn’t mess with death.

That MRI death scene…
---------------------

![Image 3: Richard Harmon as Erik and Owen Joyner as Bobby](blob:http://localhost/30990b17de217b0e1b31c81af93b81ea)

Left to right: Richard Harmon as Erik, Owen Joyner as Bobby. Credit: Warner Bros. UK & Ireland.

The filmmakers were definitely creative with their kills on this one. If you’ve seen any _Final Destination_ movie, you’d know that there are exceptions to cheating death, though risky. Erik tries this trick with Bobby in the hospital when visiting [William Bludworth](https://deadline.com/2025/05/final-destination-bloodlines-tony-todd-bittersweet-goodbye-1236392591/), a recurring character of the series. Taking advantage to Bobby’s nut allergy, Erik plans to momentarily kill his brother and then resuscitate him so that Death will skip him.

Unfortunately, this backfires and Erik gets the most brutal death of the movie. It’s important to note that unlike the other Campbells, Erik was the only one not targeted in the face area. For example, his father, Mr. Campbell took a lawn mower to the face; then, his sister Julia’s head got crushed inside a garbage truck; Bobby’s head got impaled by a vending machine spring; Darlene got hit in the head by a pole; and finally the Reyes siblings got impaled in the head by two logs at the end of the film. These similar deaths are a reference to how Iris died in the premonition and in front of Stefani.

The Campbell’s deaths are all connected, except for Erik’s because he isn’t a Campbell. This makes his death scene the most memorable and, of course, separates his character from everybody else. Even the large skull tattoo on his torso was intentional, referencing the skull imagery on the prior _Final Destination_ movies. As Erik is sandwiched into the machine, the metal tubes of a wheelchair impale the skull on his torso, referencing the _Final Destination_ 5 poster.

On that note, Erik’s death might just be the most gruesome death in the franchise so far. His piercings being ripped off by the magnetic pull of the MRI before being crushed– it’s like the [log scene](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uPCH45VxIDs) all over again. But one particular part of that scene was Harmon’s idea, the one that made us all wince. “Looking at this character and the way that he’s tattooed and the way that he’s pierced, I said ‘there’s another piercing, you know,’ and they’re like, ‘What do you mean?’ ‘I think you know exactly what I mean,'” Harmon said about the [MRI scene.](https://www.businessinsider.com/final-destination-bloodlines-mri-scene-richard-harmon-2025-5)

Erik Campbell
-------------

_"Maybe death's not actually coming for our family... 'cause that would be fucking crazy."_
**Erik to [Stefani Reyes](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Stefani_Reyes "Stefani Reyes") and [Charlie Reyes](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Charlie_Reyes "Charlie Reyes").**

**Erik Campbell** is a main character in the film _[Final Destination Bloodlines](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Final\_Destination\_Bloodlines "Final Destination Bloodlines")_. He is a child of [Brenda Campbell](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Brenda_Campbell "Brenda Campbell") and a step-grandson of [Paul](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Paul_Campbell "Paul Campbell") and [Iris Campbell](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Iris_Campbell "Iris Campbell"), the latter of whom was a visionary who prevented [The Sky View](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/The_Sky_View "The Sky View") collapse that would have occurred in 1969. Later, he is revealed to be the child of Brenda and [Jerry Fenbury](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Jerry_Fenbury "Jerry Fenbury") as a result of an affair.

Erik was the by-product of an affair, therefore not part of the Campbell bloodline, but was added to the list due to trying to assist [Bobby](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Bobby_Campbell "Bobby Campbell") in surviving Death.

_Biography_[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Ffinaldestination.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FErik_Campbell%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Erik was assumed to be the eldest son of [Howard](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Howard_Campbell "Howard Campbell") and [Brenda Campbell](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Brenda_Campbell "Brenda Campbell"), and the older brother of [Bobby](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Bobby_Campbell "Bobby Campbell") and [Julia Campbell](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Julia_Campbell "Julia Campbell"). He is also the cousin of [Stefani](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Stefani_Reyes "Stefani Reyes") and [Charlie Reyes](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Charlie_Reyes "Charlie Reyes"). His grandmother is [Iris](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Iris_Campbell "Iris Campbell")—the woman who had a premonition in 1969 that saved several lives and triggered Death targeting the Campbell bloodline. Later, he is revealed to be the product of an affair between Jerry and Brenda, making him, biologically, the older half-brother of Bobby and Julia, and not related to Iris through bloodline.

_Personality_[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Ffinaldestination.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FErik_Campbell%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Erik works as a tattoo artist. He has a rebellious and bold personality. He wears black clothes, has many piercings and tattoos, and has a sarcastic sense of humor. He doesn't believe in the supernatural and often makes fun of the idea that Death has a design or pattern. However, deep down, Erik is very protective of his family, especially Bobby and Stefani. Even though he acts like he doesn't care, he tries to keep them safe in his own way.

_Final Destination Bloodlines_[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Ffinaldestination.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FErik_Campbell%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D3&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Erik is playing _Mortal Kombat 1_ when [Bobby](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Bobby_Campbell "Bobby Campbell") interrupts him and urges him to help find his pet turtle, [Paco](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Paco "Paco"). Erik is annoyed and dismissive of his brother's worries and gets angry when Bobby continues to interfere with his gaming session, telling Bobby that he's in a ranked match. Just then, [Stefani](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Stefani_Reyes "Stefani Reyes") and [Charlie Reyes](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Charlie_Reyes "Charlie Reyes") arrive, which surprises the two. Erik is informed by Charlie that Stefani isn't doing well in college. He happily tells Stefani that he didn't do well either and tries to help Bobby find Paco.

[![Image 1: Erik calls Iris "psycho granny"](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/9/95/Erik_closeup_face_2.PNG/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/177?cb=20250602073837)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/9/95/Erik_closeup_face_2.PNG/revision/latest?cb=20250602073837)

Erik calls Iris "psycho granny"

Later, Stefani asks Erik's parents about their grandma Iris, to which Howard says that Iris is a very disturbed woman. When Bobby, Erik, and Julia join them, Erik is holding a golf club and asks what they're talking about. Charlie informs him that Stefani is dreaming about Iris, whom Erik proceeds to call "psycho granny." Charlie finds Paco in the refrigerator, and Erik tells them that Paco would enjoy being in the living room. Afterwards, Stefani goes to find Iris, where she witnesses her die in a freak accident. Not long after, Erik, along with his and Stefani's family, attends Iris' funeral. There, he is smacked by Julia on the arm after he asks Stefani an inconsiderate question about Iris' death, which he subsequently apologizes for.

[![Image 2: Erik at the barbecue](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/8/85/Eriklookingdamnfine.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/147?cb=20250325164050)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/8/85/Eriklookingdamnfine.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20250325164050)

Erik at the barbecue

Afterwards, the entire family meets for a barbecue, where Erik is placed in charge of the grill. When [Darlene](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Darlene_Campbell "Darlene Campbell") arrives at the barbecue, Erik puts his bottle of [Hice Pale Ale](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Hice_Pale_Ale "Hice Pale Ale") on the outdoor fireplace. Darlene has made cookies, and after Charlie takes a bite, he asks if there's peanut butter in it, and she confirms. Erik asks if she's trying to kill Bobby, and she remembers that Bobby is allergic. Howard gives a toast to the entire family, and they drink from their glasses. Later on, he, [Marty](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Marty_Reyes "Marty Reyes"), Howard, and Julia all play Jenga until Howard gets called to jump on the trampoline in the garden by Bobby. Stefani later arrives to see if everyone is alright. A chain reaction causes Howard's face to be shredded by a lawnmower. Erik and Marty run to stop the lawnmower, but it's too late.

After Howard's funeral, Erik and the rest of the family are gathered by Stefani, where they are informed of [Death's design](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Death%27s_design "Death's design"). Julia tells Stefani that they aren't connected to the deaths of other people, and Erik agrees with her. After Bobby starts to understand Stefani's theory, Erik stops him from believing her. Stefani proceeds to tell the family about their place on Death's list. Erik is told that he should be the second to die in Howard's bloodline, and in response, he gives his cousin the middle finger and tells her to go fuck herself. After hearing Stefani's explanation, Erik asks Charlie if he believes in Stefani, to which he replies, saying he's unsure. Tearful, Brenda starts to leave, and others follow suit. Before Erik leaves, Stefani warns him and is concerned about his safety. He tells her to stop and leaves to comfort his mother.

Later that night, Erik is at the tattoo parlor, working as a favor for his boss. He is told that he has to lock up for the night, and he complains. After Erik finishes giving a customer a tongue piercing inside the tattoo parlor, he goes over to close the shop for the night. Before he leaves, he cleans his tattoo bed with a flammable "Multi-Surface Disinfectant Spray" as he turns on his ceiling fan, which spins dangerously close to some hanging chains. He checks his phone and sees Stefani worrying over him. He tells her to stop bothering him and that he's trying to sleep.

After seeing a photo of him and his father, wanting to remember him after he passed away, he went over to work on a tattoo for himself. Along with this, he puts on a song from a playlist titled "Erik's Sad Mix". The mix plays Air Supply's "Without You". Death then begins to use the items to claim Erik's life. As the song plays with the sound system, the vibrations from the subwoofer cause a bobblehead skeleton situated on it to fall from its place, colliding with other materials before causing a glass jar full of needles/pins to fall and shatter on the floor, causing a loud sound.

[![Image 3: Erik after his nose piercing gets caught](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/e/e7/Erik%27s_piercing_gets_caught.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/260?cb=20250616032409)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/e/e7/Erik%27s_piercing_gets_caught.png/revision/latest?cb=20250616032409)

Erik after his nose piercing gets caught

Due to the sound, Erik gets up to check and proceeds to clean the mess, but pushes his chair a bit too hard, which hits the gallon of isopropyl alcohol. After it fell over, Death opens it to spill the IPA. Before realizing what else has fallen, a chain from the ceiling breaks and falls, attaching itself to Erik's nose ring. Erik is briefly shocked and tries to detach the chain.

However, he soon starts to panic as he notices the chain beginning to wrap itself around the fan, pulling him up closer to the ceiling. Erik struggles to free himself and tries to balance on a chair, failing to detach the chain. As it becomes increasingly more painful, he tries to partially stand elsewhere but accidentally knocks over a lamp into the spilled disinfectant spray, causing it to start a fire a few feet away from him.

[![Image 4: Erik being burned in fire](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/5/5b/Erik_burning_in_fire.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/280?cb=20250308043322)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/5/5b/Erik_burning_in_fire.png/revision/latest?cb=20250308043322)

Erik being burned in fire

Now desperate, he tries to stand on a glass display case, but it breaks under his weight, forcing him to move to the nearby tattoo bed. The fan slowly breaks apart as he helplessly tries to balance himself on the bed. It finally breaks as he swings towards the fire, pulling the fan out of its socket and making him fall into the flames that proceed to engulf him. He is also branded by a heart piercing that fell earlier.

However, Erik manages to survive due to his leather clothing protecting him from the flames. The next morning, he is almost hit by a car and expresses disappointment when realizing that it is Stefani and Charlie. The two are confused after hearing about the tattoo parlor burning down, and Stefani is relieved to see him alive. He shows them the heart branding on his arm and rebukes her constant messaging late last night. Stefani then expresses confusion about him surviving, and he reassures them that Death isn't coming after their family, calling the idea crazy before almost getting hit by a delivery van.

Afterwards, he informs them that maybe he is invincible. Erik continues to walk, and Stefani tells him to avoid various things that could kill him. He mocks her, and Julia walks out of his family's home. She is concerned once she notices his injuries, but he waves her off. After Stefani tells him to stay away from the garbage truck next to him, he goes to take provocative actions towards the truck. Julia leaves to jog, and Erik angrily tells Stefani that their family isn't in any danger. A chain of events causes Julia to fall into the garbage truck's compactor, and the trio chases after it. Erik manages to get in front of the truck and causes the driver to stop. But it's too late, and Julia is crushed to death.

[![Image 5: Erik is informed that Jerry Fenbury is his real father](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/3/39/Erik_finds_out_his_real_father.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/240?cb=20250617114335)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/3/39/Erik_finds_out_his_real_father.png/revision/latest?cb=20250617114335)

Erik is informed that Jerry Fenbury is his real father

Mourning Julia's death, Stefani blames herself for getting the order wrong. However, Brenda reveals that Stefani is not to blame as she had an affair that caused Erik's birth, meaning Erik was never on Death's list. Erik is confused, asking his mother who his real father is. She reveals that it is [Jerry Fenbury](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Jerry_Fenbury "Jerry Fenbury"), and he storms off with Brenda following, remarking on that being the reason why Jerry always wanted to play catch.

The rest of the family figures out that Bobby is next to die and that a person named "[JB](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/William_Bludworth "William Bludworth")" at [Hope River Hospital](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Hope_River_Hospital "Hope River Hospital") knows someone who was on Death's list and survived. They gather outside and prepare to head to the hospital. Before leaving, Erik comes out of the house and informs Darlene to get rid of the peanut butter. He contemplates for a moment and decides that he's coming with them to keep Bobby safe from harm.

Arriving at the hospital, Erik reassures Bobby. After he goes through the revolving doors, the family makes it to the morgue and meets "JB". He reveals himself to be William Bludworth and informs the family about his connection to Iris, being a fellow survivor who escaped The Sky View. The family asks him how they are able to get off of Death's list. He informs them that the only way is to either kill someone and take their remaining lifespan or successfully resuscitate a person on the list, which a previous [survivor](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Kimberly_Corman "Kimberly Corman") has done before. William then leaves, and the family is distraught. Erik suggests killing and resuscitating Bobby to get the entire family off of Death's list; however, they are against the idea. Bobby asks Stefani if there's any other way, and she tells him that it's over. Erik pulls Bobby aside and tells him that Stefani has given up on him, but he's not going to.

[![Image 6: Erik and Bobby are against harming the babies](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/b/b1/Erik_and_Bobby_look_at_babies.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/266?cb=20250617114526)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/b/b1/Erik_and_Bobby_look_at_babies.png/revision/latest?cb=20250617114526)

Erik and Bobby are against harming the babies

Afterwards, the two leave, and Erik hatches a plan to resuscitate Bobby, then send him to the ER. Bobby is skeptical of the idea, and Erik suggests that Bobby kill someone to take their life. Erik doesn't like the idea, as they have no way of knowing how much time that person has left. Right next to them, they see a NICU station through a window. Erik is against it, but considers it, and Bobby immediately shoots him down.

Right after, Erik tells Bobby that he has a plan and that it's "a little nuts." They head to a vending machine, and Erik tells Bobby that he'll use his deadly nut allergy to kill and resuscitate him. They pick a flavor, but the machine malfunctions. Erik is frustrated and begins to rock the machine, which makes a spring come loose.

### Death[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Ffinaldestination.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FErik_Campbell%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D4&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

Now having the snack, they head into a scan room where Erik leaves Bobby to find a wheelchair. After he exits, a clipboard in the control room falls onto a computer key that activates the MRI machine. Bobby notices the machine's lights turn on, though he does not do anything more than look. When Erik returns with the wheelchair, he informs Bobby about his plan to use the new life method that William mentioned. He tells him to eat the peanut snack and to sit in the wheelchair so that he can stop breathing and be rushed to the nearest doctor.

Unbeknownst to them both, the Tesla power of the machine's magnet has been slowly increasing to a dangerously powerful level. Before Bobby eats the snack, he makes Erik promise that if he dies, he will take care of Paco. Erik reassures Bobby that he and their family will survive. Bobby then eats the snack and shows no reaction. Erik gets frustrated, but Bobby begins to choke and, in his panic, reaches for his EpiPen and falls next to the door. Erik tells Bobby to sit back in the wheelchair, but a magnet swiftly pulls Erik's phone towards the override button. He turns towards the machine, noticing that it is also pulling his piercings. Erik then screams as each one is forcefully ripped from his body. His ear piercings are removed first, followed by the one on his nose, then his nipples, and lastly his groin.

[![Image 7: Erik is fatally impaled by the wheelchair](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/c/cc/ErikDeath2.gif/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/245?cb=20250616140354)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/finaldestination/images/c/cc/ErikDeath2.gif/revision/latest?cb=20250616140354)

Erik is fatally impaled by the wheelchair

The wheelchair is pulled into the MRI machine after the magnet's power exceeds 5 teslas. In the process, the wheelchair pushes Erik torso-first towards the tunnel's opening. His spine bends backward as the magnetic fields become more powerful. The strong magnetic force breaks the wheelchair; it detaches the spokes from the wheel's rim, and the spokes impale Erik through the chest. Erik dies as his body folds in half, suffering a crush injury when the wheelchair finally forces him inside the MRI's bore.

#### Signs/Clues[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Ffinaldestination.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FErik_Campbell%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D5&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

*   Erik tells his boss to "burn in hell" after he tells him to close the parlor, a sign of Erik's near-death experience, having to do with the fire that almost burned him to death. 
    *   When barbequing before Howard's death, there was a flare-up that startled Erik.

*   In the neighborhood scene, when Erik mocks Stefani’s warning, he lewdly humps the garbage truck. Notably, he does this while standing directly above a large garbage truck wheel, which resembles the circular shape of an MRI machine. This visual subtly foreshadows his eventual death.
*   The time on Erik’s phone is currently 1:13; 13 is an unlucky number.
*   A dummy figure can be seen with a needle on its nose, and right next to it is a bobblehead of a skeleton figure holding a candle. Skeletons are known to be common figures or representations of death.
*   There is a raven statuette on the desk. Ravens are sometimes seen as dark omens and feed on deceased animals.
*   There are three neon signs in the tattoo parlor: 
    *   One is in the shape of a snake with a lightning bolt behind it.
    *   The other is a horseshoe magnet.
    *   And the last one is a skull on fire at one of the windows facing the street.

*   Several of Erik’s music playlists subtly hint at his death: 
    *   **Screaming in the Void:** When he dies, he screams in pain inside an empty room, literally a “void-like” space.
    *   **Iteration Station:** The incident at the tattoo shop functions as an “iteration station,” meaning the sequence of [death list](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Death_list "Death list") is reset there.
    *   The skull icon beneath the “Iteration Station” playlist symbolizes death.

*   There are car lights on the wall, hinting at him almost getting run over twice.
*   The number on the tattoo parlor's glass door is 1969, the year when the Sky View collapse would have occurred.
*   Items made of glass broke during Erik's accident, similar to what happened in the Sky View Tower incident and his father's death: 
    *   A glass jar breaks next to Erik.
    *   The glass display case cracks under Erik's feet.
    *   He cracks the glass on the vending machine by hitting it.

*   The chain that got caught in the ceiling fan pulled Erik upwards by his nose piercing, and later in the MRI room, his nose piercing would also be similarly pulled from him.
*   Erik's tattoo on the torso and right hand has a skull on it, with skulls often being a symbol of [Death](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Death "Death").
*   Erik alludes to how his plan to kill and revive Bobby would be "a little nuts".
*   After the tattoo parlor fire, Stefani and Charlie drive to Erik's house to see if he's alright. After they nearly hit him with Stefani's car, Erik yells, "Are you trying to kill me?!"
*   As Darlene tries to remember the hospital where JB resides, she mentions a name that sounds like "piece ripper".
*   MRI Redirect "Magnetic Resonance Imaging".
*   When Erik leaves the MRI room to fetch the wheelchair, Bobby watches the MRI switch on and pull its bed into the bore, like it will with Erik soon after.
*   As Erik runs off with the wheelchair, there's a video that lists various metal objects that can be attracted to the MRI machine. One of the items listed is _piercings_.

*   Erik's death is similar to the death of [Candice Hooper](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Candice_Hooper "Candice Hooper"); both are killed while snapping their spines.
*   The _[Final Destination 5](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Final\_Destination\_5 "Final Destination 5")_ poster is referenced by Erik's skull tattoo following his impalement by a wheelchair.
*   [Clear Rivers](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Clear_Rivers "Clear Rivers") and Erik wore leather clothing during fire-related accidents. Even though Clear was killed on impact, Erik manages to survive the incident.
*   Erik's [_**coffee mug**_](https://youtu.be/lcpODbHYElo?t=63) says "Show me your kitties", which is a small nod to [Frankie Cheeks](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Frankie_Cheeks "Frankie Cheeks")'s infamous quote "Show me your titties," which he told to [Ashley](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Ashley_Freund "Ashley Freund") and [Ashlyn](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Ashlyn_Halperin "Ashlyn Halperin") at the [Devil's Flight](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Devil%27s_Flight "Devil's Flight") ride in _[Final Destination 3](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Final\_Destination\_3 "Final Destination 3")._
*   In the family barbecue scene, he makes a small reference to the death of [Brian Gibbons](https://finaldestination.fandom.com/wiki/Brian_Gibbons "Brian Gibbons"), who died while at a family barbecue.
*   In the original script, Erik was called **Derek**.

The Campbell-Reyes Bloodline
----------------------------

Stefani Reyes

Stefani Reyes
-------------

![Image 1: Characters in Final Destination Bloodlines](https://mediaproxy.tvtropes.org/width/1200/https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/steph_5.png)

_"I'm not like her, okay? I'm not crazy."_

### **Played By:** Kaitlyn Santa Juana

A young college student who happens to receive her grandmother Iris's vision of the Sky View disaster. Her investigation leads her to learn that most of her family are on Death's List, forcing her to find a way to stop Death before he gets them all.

* * *

*   [Aloof Big Sister](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AloofBigSister "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AloofBigSister"): [Charlie used to look up to Stefani as a kid](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigSisterWorship "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigSisterWorship"), but after she went to college, she always brushed his attempts to reach out to her. Charlie ultimately gave up, coming to the conclusion that she didn't care about her family anymore.
*   [All Up to You](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AllUpToYou "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AllUpToYou"): After visiting her grandmother along with witnessing her demise by Death's hand, Stefani takes it on herself to use her newfound knowledge to protect her family however she can.
*   [Badass Bookworm](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BadassBookworm "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BadassBookworm"): Downplayed, but she shows some courage and athleticism while trying to protect Julia and Charlie and got good grades before her visions.
*   [Blessed with Suck](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BlessedWithSuck "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BlessedWithSuck"): She's cursed with nightmares about the Sky View tragedy which have negatively impacted her college standing. She is also able to pick up on Death's presence and uses it to warn her family members with minimal success.
*   [Blood-Splattered Innocents](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BloodSplatteredInnocents "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BloodSplatteredInnocents"): When she tries to leave Iris' house after being disturbed by her statements about Death, Iris proves the curse is real by allowing herself to be impaled by a weather vane right in front of Stefani, drenching her face in blood.
*   [Brainy Brunette](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrainyBrunette "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrainyBrunette"): She has dark brown hair inherited from the Filipino side of her family tree. Charlie mentioned that she had been valedictorian in school; yet, aside from her supposed academic capabilities, she's quite savvy and perceptive as shown  when she predicts the sequence of events Death triggers to claim Julia, and later, Darlene.
*   [Broken Bird](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrokenBird "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrokenBird"): Her estrangement from her family members and months of traumatic nightmares that disrupt her education and social life have left her high-strung and lonely even before she learns of the curse and starts seeing her family die one-by-one in front of her in the midst of repairing their relationship.
*   [Damsel in Distress](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DamselInDistress "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DamselInDistress"): In [The Climax](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheClimax "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheClimax"), she's stuck in her seat as the RV starts to sink underwater which leads to her drowning. Thankfully, her brother is able to save her. Too bad she was only unconscious, so she wasn't skipped.

*   [Closest Thing We Got](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ClosestThingWeGot "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ClosestThingWeGot"): In the vision, he is the only person on hand with even the slightest amount of authority or knowledge to coordinate the evacuation, and while he does direct the patrons and staff to the stairs, a safer alternative in emergencies like this, when the stairs cave in, he's got no choice but to use the elevator.
*   [Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CrouchingMoronHiddenBadass "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CrouchingMoronHiddenBadass"): [Downplayed](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DownplayedTrope "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DownplayedTrope"). Despite some irresponsible moments, he does a brave and level-headed attempt to evacuate as many people via the elevator as safely as possible in Iris' vision. Unfortunately, too many people inside the elevator and the faulty structure of the shaft render his efforts [All for Nothing](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AllForNothing "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AllForNothing").
*   [Didn't Think This Through](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DidntThinkThisThrough "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DidntThinkThisThrough"): Before the tragedy took place, he didn't seem to mind having extra people go into the elevator nor does he realize that the doors jamming would be an issue worth evaluating.
*   [Elevator Failure](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ElevatorFailure "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ElevatorFailure"): In the original timeline, he and many of the patrons were meant to die from the elevator crashing downwards.
*   [Get Out!](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GetOut "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GetOut"): He demands the Host to exit the elevator as it's already over capacity, but it wouldn't have done any good, as the elevator gives way, sending him and the patrons inside to their deaths below in the premonition.
*   [Killed Offscreen](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KilledOffscreen "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KilledOffscreen"): Sadly, due to Death's design, he's bitten it way before the events of the movie. The same also applies to his intended death as we never see him or the other guests become pancakes after the crash.
*   [Mr. Exposition](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MrExposition "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MrExposition"): He tells Iris and Paul all about the building of the Sky View, which includes construction details that will contribute to its destruction.
*   [Nice Guy](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NiceGuy "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NiceGuy"): He seems helpful and cordial with the guests regardless of class status.
*   [Tempting Fate](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TemptingFate "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TemptingFate"): He tells Iris it is fine to get in the overloaded elevator and ride up to the restaurant. During the disaster, he is left vainly yelling to the crowd that too many people are getting on the elevator and the extra weight will kill them all.

The Piano Lady

Daphne Wo
---------

![Image 16: https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/msdaphne.png](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/msdaphne.png)

### **Played By:** Megan Hui

A Sky View patron who was meant to lose more than just her hat at the restaurant.

* * *

*   [Babies Ever After](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BabiesEverAfter "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BabiesEverAfter"): A news article reveals she lived long enough to have a daughter named Amelia (although her being around her late thirties during the disaster makes it possible she had older children born before she became targeted), who would later die from falling off a cliff at a nature reserve.
*   [Destination Defenestration](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DestinationDefenestration "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DestinationDefenestration"): She meets her end in the vision when a falling piano smashes her out the windows she and several other people were leaning against. She may also be the survivor who a newspaper article mentions dying years later from falling off a balcony.
*   [Hope Spot](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HopeSpot "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HopeSpot"): In the vision, Iris was almost able to grab her hand before she fell down and landed against a window, right in the path of a precariously teetering piano...
*   [Killed Offscreen](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KilledOffscreen "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KilledOffscreen"): She's already dead before the events of the movie due to Death's design.
*   [Oh, Crap!](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OhCrap "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OhCrap"): In the vision, she screams in horror when she sees the piano hurtling towards her.
*   [Stylish Sunhats](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StylishSunhats "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StylishSunhats"): She wore a fancy red hat that got blown over the Sky View's balcony from a gust of wind. The fact that she nearly fell over the railing trying to retrieve it ends up foreshadowing how she would die for real.

The Fullers

Beatrice Fuller and Mr. Fuller
------------------------------

![Image 17: https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/brushedoffforthem.png](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/brushedoffforthem.png)

### **Played By:** Yvette Ferguson (Beatrice) and Mark Brandon (Mr. Fuller)

A pair of wealthy socialites who reserve a table for doom.

* * *

*   [Ambiguously Related](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AmbiguouslyRelated "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AmbiguouslyRelated"): They share a surname with one of the visionaries of _[Final Destination: Destination Zero](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Literature/FinalDestinationDestinationZero "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Literature/FinalDestinationDestinationZero")_ (herself a descendant of the other visionary from that book, who lived in Victorian times), although any children Mrs. Fuller might have given birth to would have had to have been born decades before the disaster.
*   [Innocently Insensitive](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InnocentlyInsensitive "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InnocentlyInsensitive"): Their happily walking into the lounge as the host gives them the table the lower-class Paul and Iris badly wanted is hardly an uplifting moment (especially combined with some haughty expressions on the trip up), but it’s not as if they pressured him to take that table away for them and they have no idea Paul is looking for a [Grand Romantic Gesture](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GrandRomanticGesture "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GrandRomanticGesture") to propose or that Iris is looking for a happy moment to admit her pregnancy.
*   [Man on Fire](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ManOnFire "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ManOnFire"): Beatrice Fuller dies by flames in both the vision and when Death catches up to her for real in the form of a house fire.
*   [No Full Name Given](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoFullNameGiven "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoFullNameGiven"): While Mrs. Fuller's first name is given as Beatrice, Mr. Fuller's first name is never given.
*   [Silver Fox](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SilverFox "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SilverFox"): They are well-dressed, well-groomed socialites who look good in their seventies.

Other Survivors and their bloodlines

*   [Aerith and Bob](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AerithAndBob "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AerithAndBob"): The three descendants of Haliee Kim with legible names are Leo, Ava, and Harki.
*   [Alliterative Family](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AlliterativeFamily "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AlliterativeFamily"):
    *    The eldest child of Loki Lee is named Lucas.
    *    The eldest child of Miles Miller is named Michelle.
    *    Three of the five descendants of Benjamin Parker have "c" names: Crystal, Caitlyn, and Corey.

*   [All Relatives Share a Surname](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AllRelativesShareASurname "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AllRelativesShareASurname"): Played straight with several of the families in the clipping book but subverted with others (not unlike with Iris's descendants themselves). Peter Rock's son shares his surname, but his four daughters all have the last name Miller. The two children of Lloyd Howard are Sophia Wang and Chelsea Howard. And two of Mary Jansens four children and three of her grandchildren have different surnames (Banks and Henry).
*   [Ambiguous Situation](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AmbiguousSituation "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AmbiguousSituation"):
    *    Iris has a newspaper clipping about the lives and contrived deaths of Jackson Williams and his twin sons Malcom and Manny Shepherds (who survived a train wreck mysteriously unscathed and then were killed one by one over less than a week several years later), but has no family tree drawing for them like she does for the other Sky View bloodlines. This could be a simple continuity error, indicate Jackson was an illegitimate child of a survivor she never positively identified, or mean that she initially thought their ill fortune marked them as a Sky View bloodline before realizing she was wrong.
    *    There is a sticky note with the name Brandy Whyne over an obituary for a woman named Betty Edwards who was killed just before her wedding. Whether Iris marked that wrong or Brandy changed her name (whether to hide from Death, in early anticipation of her marriage, or for more mundane reasons) is unclear.
    *    It is faintly possible a few kids in certain family trees were born before the disaster and never targeted and that Iris was initially unaware of that due to how so many survivors and descendants died in a pre-internet age where it would have been harder to trace exact ages.

*   [Amusement Park of Doom](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AmusementParkOfDoom "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AmusementParkOfDoom"): One headline involving a teenage survivor or descendant’s death references a "waterpark catastrophe," with a cutaway showing the kid drowning.
*   [Art Attacker](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArtAttacker "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArtAttacker"): Death killed Steven Williams in something the newspapers call a "statue mishap."
*   [Bus Crash](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BusCrash "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BusCrash"): Iris and Bludworth indicate that every one of them died between the prologue and the [Time Skip](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TimeSkip "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TimeSkip").
*   [Dad the Veteran](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DadTheVeteran "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DadTheVeteran"): Paul Clarke is seen in a family photo with two little girls and is described as a [World War II](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/UsefulNotes/WorldWarII "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/UsefulNotes/WorldWarII") hero in his obituary.
*   [Family Theme Naming](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FamilyThemeNaming "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FamilyThemeNaming"):
    *    Wei, Mei, and Lia Chan all have three-letter names with an "i" and another vowel in them.
    *    The youngest daughter of Belinda Banks is named Wanda, both names that end with "nda."
    *    Brandy and Sheri Whyne may have their names derived from the types of alcohol brandy and sherry.
    *    The names of Michelle and Courtney Miller may come from how Michelle is the middle name of [Courtney Love](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Music/CourtneyLove "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Music/CourtneyLove").

*   [Forklift Fu](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ForkliftFu "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ForkliftFu"): One survivor or descendant working as a manager at a canned goods company is killed by an out-of-control forklift.
*   [Ground by Gears](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GroundByGears "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GroundByGears"): One entire family got dragged into the teeth of some large industrial machine.
*   [Hope Spot](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HopeSpot "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HopeSpot"):
    *    Bradley Fitz, a lawyer and survivor, made it onto a fire escape in the face of some danger when Death came for him, then fell off of it to his death.
    *    An unnamed skateboarder initally survives a fall or collision but then dies at the hospital.
    *    Jackson Williams and his sons survived a train crash, but Death had other plans for them years later.

*   [Humble Hero](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HumbleHero "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HumbleHero"): Paul Clarke’s obituary calls him an unsung war hero, likely making him this.
*   [Named Like My Name](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NamedLikeMyName "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NamedLikeMyName"): A variant occurs with Pat Jansen, who suddenly ends up having a name similar to Founding Father Patrick Henry after marrying a man whose surname is Henry.
*   [Nom de Mom](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NomDeMom "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NomDeMom"): The Shepherds Twins seem to have their mother’s last name, as their father is Jackson Williams.
*   [Old Maid](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OldMaid "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OldMaid"): The [Big Board](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigBoard "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigBoard") picture of Brenda Smithe, one of the most recent victims and the daughter of survivor Scott Smithee, is that of a wrinkly old woman, and the family tree chart indicates she never had any descendants.
*   [One-Steve Limit](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OneSteveLimit "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OneSteveLimit"):
    *    Sky View daughter Sandy Williams and grandson Sandy Jansen share their [Gender-Blender Name](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GenderBlenderName "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GenderBlenderName") despite there being no known connection between their families besides the accident. Coincidentally, both get a [Death from Above](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DeathFromAbove "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DeathFromAbove"), via bridge debris and a cable car, respectively.
    *    Not only do survivor descendants Ava Kim and Ava Carnes share a given name, but both have a c/k surname and siblings with similar sounding given names (Leo Kim and Leia Carnes).
    *    Paul Clarke has the same given name and surname initial as Paul Campbell, the heroine's grandfather.

*   [Sibling Team](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SiblingTeam "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SiblingTeam"): Matt and Felix Waters falling from a [Rope Bridge](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RopeBridge "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RopeBridge") together indicates they did things together off the beaten path.

Others
------

Val

Val
---

![Image 18: https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/valeria_6.png](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/valeria_6.png)

### **Played By:** Breanna Llewlyn

Stefani’s roommate who's in desperate need of sleep.

* * *

*   [Enlightened Self-Interest](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EnlightenedSelfInterest "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EnlightenedSelfInterest"): She wants Stefani to go talk to her family for peace of mind out of concern for her friend but also makes it clear that wanting to get a good night’s sleep herself away from Stefani’s night terrors also matters in her advice-giving mindset.
*   [Girly Girl](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GirlyGirl "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GirlyGirl"): She has a pink shirt, stuffed animals, and a looser hairstyle than her studious roomate.
*   [Hidden Depths](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HiddenDepths "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HiddenDepths"): In spite of her blunt attitude towards Stefani, Val does seem to value friendships as the side of her dorm is decorated with polaroids of herself alongside many friends, and the way Stefani is able to laugh about Val's blunter coments suggests she sees Val as a [Morality Pet](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MoralityPet "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MoralityPet") even amidst her isolation.
*   [Ms. Exposition](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MsExposition "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MsExposition"): Her conversation with Stefani helps inform the audience about the nature, duration, and detrimental effects of Stefani’s nightmarish visions, as well as her estrangement from her family.
*   [Unwitting Instigator of Doom](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/UnwittingInstigatorOfDoom "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/UnwittingInstigatorOfDoom"): She's arguably this, as her convincing Stefani to go home and talk to her family about her nightmares sets the movie's events into motion. However, it could be subverted since Iris was already dying of cancer, so all Val really did was indirectly make Stefani aware of Death's plan for her and her family.

Mo

Mo
--

![Image 19: https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/truckerdude.png](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/truckerdude.png)

### **Played By:** Sean C. Orr

A garbage truck driver who's looking to get lucky.

* * *

*   [Headphones Equal Isolation](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HeadphonesEqualIsolation "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HeadphonesEqualIsolation"): While wearing headphones jamming to [Kelly Clarkson](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Music/KellyClarkson "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Music/KellyClarkson")'s "Stronger", he fails to hear Julia being trapped in his truck’s compactor and the aspiring rescuers yelling for him to stop because he is listening to music.
*   [I Just Want to Be Loved](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/IJustWantToBeLoved "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/IJustWantToBeLoved"): He longs for love as he browses through different women on a Tinder app (called Grinder) while working and listening to love songs.
*   [Unwitting Pawn](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/UnwittingPawn "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/UnwittingPawn"): One of the many ordinary people who is left horrified after [being used by Death as a tool to kill his targets](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AccidentalMurder "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AccidentalMurder").
*   [What Happened to the Mouse?](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhatHappenedToTheMouse "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhatHappenedToTheMouse"): He's never seen again after his [Accidental Murder](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AccidentalMurder "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AccidentalMurder") of Julia but is most likely imprisoned for it. If he wasn’t, he was almost certainly fired for being reckless on the job.

Penny Woman

Penny Woman
-----------

![Image 20: https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/abuelita.png](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/abuelita.png)

_"Lovely day today, isn't it?"_

### **Played By:** Ethel Pitchford

A sweet old lady with quite alot of time left to live.

* * *

*   [Ambiguous Situation](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AmbiguousSituation "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AmbiguousSituation"): It isn't clear as to what business she had in the Hope Rivers Hospital in the first place.
*   [Contrasting Replacement Character](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ContrastingReplacementCharacter "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ContrastingReplacementCharacter"): To the original Penny Boy, Alfred Milano, since both of them are involved in Death's designs thanks to them picking up and transporting the same cursed penny. But whereas Alfred was an annoying brat from the late 1960s who stole several pennies from a fountain and willingly chucked it on top of the Sky View for cheap thrills, the Penny Woman is a friendly old lady from the present who picked the penny from the streets and unintentionally dropped it after wanting to buy lemonade from a couple of girls.
*   [Irony](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Irony "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Irony"): When meeting her, Erik makes a wisecrack about her having "much time left". She ends up outliving him and his cousins.
*   [Nice Girl](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NiceGirl "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NiceGirl"): A friendly old woman who likes to make conversation and supports local businesses run by hard-working girls.
*   [No Name Given](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoNameGiven "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoNameGiven"): There's no word on what her official name is.
*   [Small Role, Big Impact](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SmallRoleBigImpact "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SmallRoleBigImpact"): She only appears in a handful of scenes. But it's through her picking up a penny which leads to the deaths of Stephani and Charlie Reyes (and possibly countless other lives given how destructive the train crash was).
*   [Unwitting Pawn](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/UnwittingPawn "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/UnwittingPawn"): She transports the cursed penny to its designated location, a train intersection, so Death can launch his last attack on the Reyes siblings.

Jenny Reddick

Jenny Reddick
-------------

![Image 21: https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/jenn_8.png](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/jenn_8.png)

### **Played By:** Sophia Chapdelaine

Charlie’s classmate and crush.

* * *

*   [Harbinger of Impending Doom](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HarbingerOfImpendingDoom "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HarbingerOfImpendingDoom"): Her wearing a dress like Iris did at Sky View and, along with her dad, talking about the circumstances behind Stefani’s near-death experience and whether it counts as new life serve as clues about Death preparing to derail a train while coming for the Reyes siblings.
*   [Named After Someone Famous](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NamedAfterSomeoneFamous "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NamedAfterSomeoneFamous"): Jenny shares her last name with the series' creator, Jeffery Reddick. So does her father, Dr. Reddick.
*   [Nice Girl](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NiceGirl "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NiceGirl"): She has a pleasant disposition that makes it easier to see why Charlie likes her so much.
*   [Satellite Love Interest](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SatelliteLoveInterest "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SatelliteLoveInterest"): She doesn't have much characterization apart from being Charlie's lady friend.

Dr. Reddick

The father of Jenny Reddick.

* * *

*   [Mr. Exposition](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MrExposition "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MrExposition"): [Played for Horror](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PlayedForHorror "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PlayedForHorror"). He's the one who informs the Reyes siblings that Charlie saved Stefani too soon for her to cheat Death. Cue [Cruel Twist Ending](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CruelTwistEnding "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CruelTwistEnding").
*   [Named After Someone Famous](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NamedAfterSomeoneFamous "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NamedAfterSomeoneFamous"): Like with his daughter, Dr. Reddick shares his surname with Jeffery Reddick, the creator of the series.
*   [No Full Name Given](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoFullNameGiven "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoFullNameGiven"): His first name is never given.

* * *

He is a grandchild of Iris, the visionary who survived a Skyview restaurant collapse that occurred in the 1960's. He is the eldest son of Howard Campbell and Brenda Campbell. He has two younger siblings...

Erik Campbell
-------------

**Erik Campbell** is a character in the upcoming film _[Final Destination: Bloodlines](https://horror.fandom.com/wiki/Final\_Destination:\_Bloodlines\_(2025) "Final Destination: Bloodlines (2025)")_ ([2025](https://horror.fandom.com/wiki/2025 "2025")). He is a grandchild of Iris, the visionary who survived a Skyview restaurant collapse that occurred in the 1960's. 
Biography[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fhorror.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FErik_Campbell%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

He is the eldest son of Howard Campbell and Brenda Campbell. He has two younger siblings: Bobby Campbell and Julia Campbell. Erik is also the cousin of the film’s main protagonist, Stefani Lewis, and the grandson of Iris Campbell—the woman who had a premonition in 1969 that saved several lives and triggered the curse of Death targeting the Campbell bloodline,

Personallity[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fhorror.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FErik_Campbell%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Erik Campbell is a skeptical and sarcastic person who doesn’t believe in the idea of Death targeting his family, often calling it “a damn crazy idea.” He remains calm and rational, acting as the voice of reason in tense situations, but still cares deeply for his family, especially his siblings

Final Destination: Bloodlines[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fhorror.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FErik_Campbell%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D3&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Erik was the older brother of Bobby Campbell and the cousin of Stefani Reyes, who was the main protagonist of the film. All three were part of the Campbell family, which had been cursed ever since their grandmother, Iris Campbell, had a vision in 1968. That vision helped her stop the collapse of the Skyview restaurant, saving many lives but also interrupting Death’s original plan. Because of that interference, Death began hunting the Campbell bloodline decades later.

Erik worked as a tattoo artist. He had a rebellious and bold personality. He wore black clothes, had many piercings and tattoos, and had a sarcastic sense of humor. He didn’t believe in supernatural things and often made fun of the idea that Death had a design or a pattern. However, deep down, Erik was very protective of his family, especially Bobby and Stefani. Even though he acted like he didn’t care, he tried to keep them safe in his own way.

A big twist in the story revealed that Erik was not the biological son of Howard Campbell, the man everyone thought was his father. This meant that Erik was not on Death’s list at first. Because of this, he believed he was safe, which made him act more recklessly. He thought he had found a way to escape the curse, but Death eventually caught up with him.

One of Erik’s early close calls happened in his tattoo studio. He was working alone when he turned on a ceiling fan. A chain hanging from the fan got stuck in his nose ring and almost pulled him into a fire caused by spilled isopropyl alcohol. The fire spread quickly, but Erik managed to survive. His leather jacket protected him from serious burns. Even after that, he continued to deny that anything strange was happening.

Later in the film, Erik tried to cheat Death. He remembered a rule from past survivors: if someone dies and is brought back to life, the pattern can be broken. So, Erik came up with a dangerous plan. He caused a severe allergic reaction in his younger brother Bobby, planning to revive him right after. He believed this would save Bobby and stop the curse from continuing. But things went horribly wrong.

While Erik was in a hospital room, an MRI machine suddenly turned on. The strong magnetic field pulled on the metal from his piercings. Before he could escape, a wheelchair flew across the room and crushed him against the machine. Erik died instantly in a brutal and unexpected way.

Erik Campbell’s death was one of the most shocking in the movie. It showed that even those who think they are safe are still part of Death’s plan. His story was emotional and tragic.

Final Destination: Bloodlines Confirms Why Erik Died: 'Things Get Messy'
========================================================================

Final Destination: Bloodlines has no shortage of deaths, but Erik's demise stands out because of how brutal it is.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

By [Aeron Mer Eclarinal](https://thedirect.com/about/aeron-mer-eclarinal/)Posted: August 03, 2025

![Image 6: Erik in Final Destination: Bloodlines](https://images.thedirect.com/media/article_full/20250803_162113.jpg)

[_Final Destination: Bloodlines_](https://thedirect.com/tags/final-destination-bloodlines/) confirmed why Erik Campbell (Richard Harmon) died despite not being part of the family tree of Death's design. The sixth installment of the _Final Destination_ franchise dialed up the stakes when Death targeted a single family, killing them one by one due to a massive incident that did not happen in the past due to the intervention of one of their family members.

At the center of the story is Stefani Reyes (Kaitlyn Santa Juana), who has been having visions of a tragic accident that took place in the Skyview Tower in the 1960s, and the visionary is later revealed to be their grandmother, Iris (Brec Bassinger). After Iris' death in the present day, Death shifts its attention to the remaining family members, including Erik.

Directed by Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein, _Final Destination: Bloodlines_ features a stellar cast led by Brec Bassinger, Richard Harmon, Kaitlyn Santa Juana, Teo Briones, Gabrielle Rose, Owen Joyner, Anna Lore, Alex Zahara, Rya Kihlstedt, and the late Tony Todd. The movie premiered on May 16, 2025, and was later released on [HBO Max](https://thedirect.com/tags/hbo-max/) on August 1, 2025.

Why Did Erik Die In Final Destination?
--------------------------------------

![Image 7: Richard Harmon as Erik in Final Destination: Bloodlines](https://images.thedirect.com/media/photos/1erikfinaldes.png)

HBO Max

_Final Destination: Bloodlines_ revealed that Death's order is based on the Campbell family's age hierarchy, meaning that the oldest member will die first, ultimately leading to the youngest member.

After Howard Campbell's death (Iris' eldest son), the next one on the list is his eldest son, Erik Campbell. However, Erik is later seen alive and well despite almost dying inside his tattoo shop. In a shocking moment, his sister, Julia Campbell (Anna Lore), dies first, leading to confusion about Death's plan for the family.

Brenda, Erik's mother, later confirms that [he is not part of the complex Campbell family tree in _Final Destination: Bloodlines_](https://thedirect.com/article/final-destination-bloodlines-family-tree)because he is not Howard's biological son. Instead, he is the son of Jerry Fenbury, a man his mother had an affair with.

![Image 8: Richard Harmon as Erik Campbell in Final Destination: Bloodlines](https://images.thedirect.com/media/photos/2erikfinaldes.png)

HBO Max

Given Erik's safe status from Death's design, he becomes confident about saving his half-brother, Bobby, from certain doom. However, when he tries to save Bobby from his death by tricking the entity into stopping Bobby's heart with his peanut allergy, Erik is given the most brutal death in _Final Destination: Bloodlines_ after a malfunctioning MRI machine inside a hospital.

Some fans wonder why Erik died, considering he is not part of the Campbell bloodline. After he brutally dies, Stefani mumbles to herself,**"When you f*ck with death, things get messy,"**which provides the perfect explanation why Erik also died alongside Bobby.

The fact that Erik messed with Death's plan by trying to save Bobby cemented his tragic fate. In the franchise, Death is established as an intelligent force, not something to be tricked into, because the entity seems to know when someone is out to avert its plans.

The Final Destination: Bloodlines Directors Explain Why Erik Died
-----------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 9: Richard Harmon as Erik Campbell in Final Destination: Bloodlines](https://images.thedirect.com/media/photos/3erikfinaldes.png)

HBO Max

Speaking with [Polygon](https://www.polygon.com/horror/602031/final-destination-bloodlines-ending-explained-directors-spoilers-erik-death/) in May 2025, _Final Destination: Bloodlines_ directors Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein echoed the same sentiment above when they explained the reasoning behind Erik's death, with them circling back to what William Bludworth (played by the late Tony Todd) said to the Campbells in the scenes before Erik and Bobby's death:

> Adam Stein: "Tony [Todd] says it: when you fuck with death, things get messy."
> 
> 
> Zach Lipovsky: "That's right. That was our answer to that question. Right after he dies, that's the first line — ‘Why did he die?’ And Kaitlyn’s character [echoes Bludworth]: ‘When you fuck with death, things get messy.’ I think that's a very good lesson for everyone to remember."

_Final Destination: Bloodlines_ essentially explains why Erik died in the first place, and the directors point out Death's rule to remind the viewers.

But why did Death seemingly try to kill Erik inside his tattoo parlor? Stein mentioned that it is Death's**"sense of playfulness,"**comparing Erik to a fish while the entity is the fisherman who simply wants to catch him **"without intending to kill [him]:"**

> "The other big question is, why does death hook Erik in the tattoo parlor, when he's not next? We always liked the idea that death has a sense of playfulness. Just like a fisherman might catch a fish without intending to kill it, and they'll hook the fish and then throw ’em back, that's exactly what death is doing with Eric in that tattoo parlor scene."

How Death operates in _Final Destination: Bloodlines_ presents a much more difficult scenario for future victims, considering that the entity seemingly knows how to adapt and target those not planned to be part of his design (if they decide to mess with or trick Death). This should serve as a warning not to try to cheat with Death because it won't end well for any character who crosses that line.
